chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from one of our companions, from Ismail ibn Jabir
that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would recite the Azan, and someone else would recite the Iqamah, and he said, 'He would recite the Iqamah, while someone else had already recited the Azan'.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: recites the Iqamah (call to establish prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can the Imam and another person perform the Azan and Iqamah respectively during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility in the performance of the Azan and Iqamah, specifically noting that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) often delegated the Iqamah to a companion while he performed the Azan, or vice versa. This practice underscores the scholarly view that these calls are communal acts of worship rather than rigidly bound to a single reciter, facilitating ease for the congregation. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the adaptability of ritual forms to maintain congregational unity and order.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from one of our companions, from Ismail Bin Jabir that,
‘Abu Abdullahasws would recite an Azān, and someone else would recite the Iqamah, and he said, ‘When heasws recited the Iqamah, someone else would recite the Azān’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Mahziyar from certain persons of our people from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir

who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say Adhan and someone else would say ‘Iqamah.’ He (the narrator) has said that Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say ‘Iqamah and someone else would say Adhan.’”
